# Preparation Plan

Preparation Plan builds the contracts and initial state for a preparation clause identified by `clauseKey`. It extends connection planning with process refresh, document-access registration, source validation and optional participant admission. Producing a plan does not establish that a candidate document has been provided, activated, admitted or made usable.

## Configuration and connections

The planner reads the candidate clause at `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/{clauseKey}`. `type/configurableActions=true` selects `parameters/actions`; otherwise actions come from `type/actions`. `type/defaultBindings` are merged with the clause's explicit `bindings`, which take precedence. Property bindings must match `type/bindingTypes`; a `pointer` must be a non-root document pointer. Only names in `type/optionalBindings` may omit their property binding. Action bindings are dictionaries of named connections, separate from data bindings. Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty and contain no dot, slash or tilde.

`type/initialState` supplies initial objects at declared pointer bindings. A clause must provide actions or structural initial state. `type/embeds` and `type/embedsCollections` identify declared pointer bindings to embed. `type/snapshotBindings` names values captured during planning: supplied snapshot paths must be text and resolve to existing data. Snapshot failure rejects planning; no snapshot is invented for an omitted binding.

Connections select `on` modes: `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `initialized`, `activated` or `timer`. Workflow connections use a named authenticated `party` or `channel`. Change and embedded sources require non-root paths; collection handlers accept only events beneath their collection path. Embedded and collection sources request embedding unless `embed=false`. An action's `automatic` connection occupies the reserved `_automatic` name. `initialized` selects Clauses Initialized; `activated` selects Document Activated.

At execution, parameters combine action `defaults`, the trigger when `input=true`, and connection `params`, followed by workflow `inputParams` and `documentParams` projections. Projection keys and values are non-root pointers; existing projected values override earlier parameters. `connectionProfiles` may supply only `params` and `when`, and cannot coexist with either field locally. Configuration remains literal during planning. `type/readParametersFromDocument=true` leaves the generated `parameters` constant empty; otherwise it contains clause parameters excluding `actions`, `conditions`, `conditionGroups` and `connectionProfiles`.

A false connection `when` skips the action. Invalid arguments, failed action `require`, or failed action conditions reject execution. Individual `parameters/conditions` default to true; applicable `conditionGroups` add conjunctive gates, with a missing group `condition` defaulting to false. Group `inputs`, when supplied, become `conditionInputs`. `requireExactDocumentVersion=true` requires an explicitly exact-reviewed workflow call.

Preflight runs before connection `before`, action `do` and connection `after`. Preflight and `resultContract="outcome-v1"` require an explicit `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped` outcome; only `acceptedNew` continues past their respective checks. The default result contract is `legacy`. `once` defaults to false. A once-only connection records `fired=true` only upon reaching its final marker, then skips subsequent attempts. This marker and `acceptedNew` describe local execution, not an external business outcome.

## Preparation refresh and source declarations

`parameters/preparationDefinition`, when present, selects its `type` as the runtime definition and must identify a Compute Definition. Otherwise the planner uses `type/actionDefinition/type`. An override replaces existing first-step definitions in the base connection plan. Canonical helper extraction is used only when the relevant functions match exactly; otherwise the full selected definition is retained.

`type/destinationBinding` names the clause binding watched for process updates. The plan initializes `/process_{clauseKey}` with `entries={}` and schedules `sharedRefresh` on destination updates, embedded events and changes to `/activation`. It also connects existing activation-access channels to `rootSourceAccessLost`.

For generated steps containing `connectionConfiguration`, source declarations combine `sources` from the selected template with each template clause's `parameters/sources`. `parameters/template` takes precedence over the captured `template` snapshot. Repeated aliases must have identical declarations or planning fails with `SOURCE_DECLARATION_CONFLICT`. Compiled matching checks the declaration for the requested alias and returns false for an unknown alias.

The supplied evidence does not include the bodies of `sharedRefresh`, `rootSourceAccessLost` or the domain-next-action helpers. Their complete refresh effects, access-loss transitions and eventual usability rules cannot be inferred from their names. The admission behavior below describes the supplied standard helpers; a selected custom definition may differ.

## Admission, consent and access

Admission contracts are added only when Activation's `parameters/admission/approvers` is nonempty. Every approver must be a declared party and occur only once. Installation initializes `admission.editable=true`, empty `grants` and `retired` maps, and a `ledger` with revision 1 and empty proposal and history maps.

A candidate requiring additional host parties enters `admission_pending`; missing admission policy rejects that case. Admission grants use an amendment proposal scoped to the candidate, parties, access evidence and Activation revision. Only one pending proposal is opened at a time. Each configured approver approves its `proposalId` through its party channel using exact document review. All approvals are required before the grant replacement is applied. An applied grant is distinct from the incoming parties' consent, access readiness and completed roster installation.

After a matching approved grant, the helper may emit Party Addition Requested and record its admission reference in `accessRequested`. This requests access processing; it does not grant access or consent. Consent operations become available only with matching grant, current Activation revision and valid access. Each incoming party's lead channel records `approve` or `decline` for the exact `admissionRef`. Repeating the same decision is a duplicate; changing a recorded decision is rejected.

Known standard stages have distinct meanings:

- `admission_pending`: waiting for admission approvals and the required access and party consents.
- `admission_denied`: a party declined.
- `reapproval_required`: the admission's Activation revision is stale.
- `installing`: all required consents, revision and access checks permit roster installation.
- `linking`: admission completed or required source links remain unready.
- `awaiting_activation`: the candidate must become active.
- `ready`: the candidate-stage checks passed; this alone does not establish final usability.
- `awaiting_provider`: an authorized rebase requires the candidate to be provided again.

`selectBeforeActivation=true` permits the candidate-stage check to bypass candidate activation, but requires its recorded configuration identity to remain current. It does not remove admission or source checks. Source linking checks initialization, declared origin, active source state and party-roster coverage.

Roster installation rejects frozen parties, stale revisions, missing policy, insufficient access and conflicting contract names. `finishAdmission` verifies roster coverage, records `admittedRevision`, sets the entry to `linking` and emits progress labeled `admitted`. That event label is not the entry's stored stage. Declined or stale admissions can retain their token, decisions and retirement reason. Rebase requires an admission approver, exact review, the current `admissionRef` and `reapproval_required`; it clears the token and consents, increments `admissionAttempt`, and requests reprovision. Its optional `key` defaults to `single`.

The plan also creates `registerAccess_{clauseKey}_{role}` operations for configured party roles. The standard implementation requires exact review and a current party-lead channel, accepting one to sixteen existing initialized Timeline Access publications. It verifies their provider, initialization history and executable policy, deduplicates by original document identity, embeds new records under `/processAccess_{clauseKey}`, and refreshes Activation. Registration does not change provider-owned access sets or establish the caller's permission to change them.

## Timers and recorded state

A timer requires exactly one of `timestamp` or `afterEvent`. Absolute `timestamp` is an integer Unix-microsecond instant from 0 through 9,007,199,254,740,991 and cannot include `delayMs` or `policy`. Relative timers require a timestamped source and a positive integer `delayMs` no greater than 9,007,199,254,740; initialization cannot supply that relative time base. `policy` defaults to `first`; `latest` permits replacement requests. Optional `cancelOn` must specify a source.

Arming emits a keyed Timer Request and records `armed=true`; cancellation emits Cancel Timer Request. The supplied handlers do not clear `armed` on cancellation or firing, so it is not a pending-timer indicator, and `first` continues to suppress later arming while it remains true. Timer requests need compatible native Time support and committed execution. A request is not a firing; deadlines must respect the invocation's logical time, and processing may occur later than wall-clock deadline time.

Process and connection paths belong to the document where this planner executes. Initial values apply only after installation. Missing fields are generally unknown, not implicit initial values. `validateConfiguration` returns allowance, while substantive configuration checks occur during planning. `validateTransition` always returns `allowed=false` with `PREPARATION_IMMUTABLE_WHILE_OBLIGATIONS_EXIST`; this function does not inspect whether obligations actually exist.
